speaker: augustine_phillips
text: That is the third time the drum has beaten the quarter-hour, and Dick has not moved his boots from the rope.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Up comes the wooden devil with his club, off goes the crown from the wooden king's head, and as soon as the cloth drops they set it on again for the next house. Nobody likes to ask him which of the two he is studying.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Every quarter-hour, Will, regular as the parish clock. Knocked off, set on again, and the same penny paid at the flap.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Come away from the rope, Dick, before you learn the wooden gesture. Did you see the constable take that cut-purse a yard from Arthur's elbow?

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: I had every word of it in my ear, Master Shakespeare. First the citizen's wife, My purse, my purse, stop the fellow in the tawny doublet. Then the thief on his knees, Good master officer, I was reaching for my own kerchief. Then the constable, Hold thy peace, knave, I have thy hand in the pocket. And the clerk behind him, Bring him to the cage, bring him to the cage.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Four voices out of one throat, and not a penny charged for the show.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Look yonder where the ring is thickest. Two hundred people standing round the dust, and there is Will Kemp in the middle of them, dancing for nothing.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A bow for my fellows, and never a box at the door. Two hundred hats around me, and not a man of them owes me a farthing for the sweat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep half a leg for tomorrow at two, Will, or Costard will limp onto the new paint.

speaker: will_kemp
text: That was only to shake the rust out of my garters. Who is the sober young citizen behind the stall of points and hat-bands, looking down his nose as if he had never seen a player?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is my brother Gilbert. Good afternoon to your stall, brother.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Points and hat-bands, gentlemen, and if you are not buying you are standing in the light of honest men who are. I know no players in Smithfield while my master's ledger is open on the board.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: God save the haberdashery. We will take our stage-coats out of your sunshine.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Go your ways to the pig-booths, brother, and mind your back in the press.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: He is right about your back, Will. We are into the fourth hour on these cobbles, and you have had your hand at your loins since the puppet booth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is complaining now. Four hours of fair-walking is enough for it. Wait. Give me three of the gingerbread men off the tray.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Three gingerbread men, Will, and one of them with gilt on his coat? Who are those for?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I had bought them before I thought. Three of them, and one with gilt on it.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Take them home to Mistress Ansell's maid, Will, and get off your feet before the crowd thickens at the gate.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Tomorrow at two of the clock. Nobody cons a line tonight.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: Mind the gilt does not rub off on your fingers, Master Shakespeare.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Go easy down by Aldersgate, Will. We'll see you before the trumpet tomorrow.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Save us a place out of the sun if you reach Shoreditch first.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Walk slow on the cobbles, Will.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Before the trumpet. Good even to you all.
